institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities due to the receiving institution being a highly acknowledged university. The second reason was that I wanted to live in Paris for a while.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:

questions.answer: Rather easily.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I found the process with OLA very exhausting and I think UCPH could have more helpful

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing with help from a private contact which made it easy, but that was very lucky and expensive too

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Prices in Paris can be high, and you will probably need to use more money on renting or otherwise compromise on location and the apartment itself

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is "first come, first served" which makes it very stressful. Be prepared for the courses you want to register for.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Videos provided to simulate a registration situation

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Rather succesful, but at Sciences Po, this process is called "Hunger Games" with good reason: You need to be very fast because spots are filliing up very very quickly.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask someone who have been at Sciences Po prior to this. Select mandatory courses first to be sure you get those.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very high workload, but the academic level was not at all higher than at my home university.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At Sciences Po, the teaching style is much more based on small classrooms with active participation from students. Much more to turn in during the semester than at UCPH. UCPH is much more pedagogical. At Sciences Po, not all teachers are great at faciliating a classroom. Generally, I like the style of teaching much better at UCPH, but it was still very enriching to try a different way for one semester

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Comparaive Politics, European Integration and its Challenges: the Euro, Migration and Populism, Green Parties and their Electorate in Europe, European Economic Law, Small and Micro States in Global Politics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked the teacher in Small and Micro States in Global Politics. Choose courses that you will not be able to particiapte in at your home university. Generally, Sciences Po have a lot of courses that allows you to study a more niche subject than what I was used to at UCPH

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. the teaching method is very different and "conservative" than that of UCPH 
2. The work load is bigger at Sciences Po. However, I do not think this should be a reason for not going to Sciences Po as it is also very enriching and challenging to try! aaand go because of Paris <3333
3. Th prepared for small classrooms where they expect oral and active participation from students

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Prepare for the process of registration for courses as this can be challenging because it is "first come, first served". Dont get scared off due to the workload. The academic level is not higher than that of UCPH.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: First of all, I have gotten some amazing friends. On the academic side, I found it very rewardig to have gained more experienced on speaking academic english in front of many people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was balancing the school obligations with the urge to just spend time in the city and enjoy. You will never be completely done with school; there will always be another text to read or another task to do. I recommend to of course do your school work, but also enjoy your weekends and evenings now that you on exchange - you will do good anyway!

questions.answer: Yes
